notes: A clean seven-bullet ladder that walks Nashmau -> Whitegate -> Nashmau, and every bullet really is an action. The only judgement call is bullet 5, "Now you must complete Cook-a-roon? for a Nashmau Stew": that is a step, not advice -- you cannot proceed without doing another quest -- so it is recorded as an obtain with no target and no zone, because the page never says where Cook-a-roon? is run from. VERIFY DROPPED the Nashmau Stew that the draft made that rung's evidence. The stew is an ordinary AH-tradeable item, and the page's own two sub-bullets say an Auction House stew and a stew kept from an earlier repeat of Cook-a-roon? will NOT work -- the warning exists precisely because players commonly already hold one. The step mark is a high-water mark over positive evidence, so a player holding a stale stew would be thrown to step 6 the moment the quest opened and pointed at Kyokyoroon while he still owed Nadee Periyaha and Cacaroon a visit. Evidence that can be true BEFORE its rung is done can only ever run the mark ahead, never make it lag, so it is worse than none: with no evidence the quest simply sits on Kakkaroon, who is also the step 7 target. The rung keeps its place; the quest now has no observable at all, hence medium. Bullets 3 and 4 are kept as two rungs on Cacaroon rather than merged, since they are two distinct actions on one marker and splitting them lets the talk show as ready before the Imperial Bronze Piece is in hand. The header's Fame field is the expansion name, "Treasures of Aht Urhgan", which the resolver folds to the Aht Urhgan region, so the region is kept.

notes: Three bullets, three steps, and the interesting one is bullet 2. The Warhorse Hoofprint is a single roaming object that appears in ONE of four zones -- Bhaflau Thickets, Caedarva Mire, Mount Zhayolm, Wajaom Woodlands -- and the page says it is visible on Widescan. That is not a group (a group means do all of them) and it is not four steps, so it is recorded as one step with a NULL zone: a zone-less row matches wherever the player happens to be, which is exactly the behaviour wanted for a target that could be in any of the four. The four zone names live in the note so nothing is lost. The header writes the giver's grid as "(1-10)", which is not a valid grid reference at all; the raw string is kept verbatim and the grid field is left null rather than guessing at (I-10). "Quest Reqs: Complete 25 points worth of Assaults as Lance Corporal" has no slot in the schema and no observable predicate, so it gates nothing and is flagged. The single "After the walkthrough" section is Related Links -- one link to a Japanese tracking wiki -- and contains no steps.

"Mog House" resolves to the moghouse sentinel and not to a zone id, and "Moogle" is one of the known ambiguous names -- an ambiguous name with no zone id is structurally forbidden (it would mark every Moogle in Vana'diel), so every step's target is deliberately none even though the page names the Moogle plainly. The zone string is still recorded as "Mog House" because that is where the quest happens and the sentinel exists for exactly this. The start NPC is left as the header's Moogle; that is the giver the page names and the start field has no such restriction. Bullet 4 is the REWARD -- the Mog Safe growing to 60 items -- written as prose about the moogle returning from a trip, so it is an outcome and not a step; that does leave the ladder ending on the trade rather than on a hand-in, which is why this is medium. None of the four is a step. The Bronze Bed, Power Bow and Beetle Ring are all in the header's Item Reqs and all three are used.

notes: Six bullets, three of which are actions. Bullet 2 (Grin shows you a picture to memorise) is part of the conversation and folds into step 1; bullet 4 (look-alike NPCs spawn on the ship) is scene-setting for step 3; bullet 6 and its two sub-bullets are the one-chance warning and the two outcomes. The quest cannot be marked past Grin: the airship passengers are never named -- naming them is the whole puzzle -- and "Airship" is not a zone the resolver knows, so step 3 has no target and no zone. That is the honest answer; inventing a passenger name or a ship zone would be exactly the guessing this pass exists to avoid. "Dropped item" is a KEY item (not an item), and the page never says when it is granted, so it is used only as a hold-requirement on the hand-in and is not evidence anywhere -- accepting the quest already tells the runtime step 1 is done. Repeatable, with three escalating titles.

The Dawn talisman is the only observable in the quest: granted by Virnage on step 2 and TAKEN BACK by Rakorok on step 5, so it is evidence on step 2 only and step 5 carries none. It is deliberately not listed as a hold-requirement on the intervening rungs either, since nothing in the page says it must be shown to anything. notes: The walkthrough never actually tells you to finish the quest. Bullet 4 says only "Complete this quest to later unlock Brygid the Stylist Returns", which is an unlock note, not an instruction -- so the return visit is read off the header's Description, "she wants you to come back wearing a robe and a bronze subligar", and cited against bullet 4. That is the one inferred rung in this batch and it is why the quest is medium; Brygid herself is named all over the page, so no name is invented, only the act of going back. Bullets 2 and 3 (buy the two pieces, then wear them) merge into one obtain rung, because holding both is the single observable and the same items cannot be evidence twice. The job list in bullet 3 is NOT a quest gate: it says which jobs can wear a Robe and a Bronze Subligar at the same time, and anyone can change job to one of them, so putting Monk/Red Mage/Thief/Bard/Dark Knight/Blue Mage into gates.jobs would hide the quest from every other job forever. It stays in the note.

notes: A two-rung repeatable trade quest whose whole content is a three-way OR, and the schema expresses it exactly: items is four Eastern Pottery, items_alt is four Northern Fur and four Southern Mummy, so any one of the three sets satisfies the rung. The three sub-bullets under bullet 2 are a drop table, and their monsters are recorded with role drop because they are what you kill to fill this rung -- but the page writes two of them in the plural ("Clockwork Pods", "Liches") and mobs are matched live by folded name, so they are recorded singular; that is a normalisation of names the page already gives, not an invention. Bullet 3 sits under a "Note:" heading and is Auction House advice, not a step. "Fame: Outlands" is not one of the nine regions -- Norg is, but the page does not say Norg -- so the region gates nothing and only the raw is kept; the level is written "1?" and the question mark is the page's own doubt.

steps.note: one set of four, your choice: Eastern Pottery pays 2000 gil (Clockwork Pods in Garlaige Citadel or Fei'Yin), Northern Fur 1500 (Giant Hunter on Qufim Island, Giant Lobber in Lower or Middle Delkfutt's Tower), Southern Mummy 3000 (Liches in Western Altepa Desert). All three are also on the Auction House under Others > Misc. 1.

notes: Four bullets, of which bullet 2 is the request restated and not a rung. The quest turns on "at least one of the three", so this is an OR and not a group: three group members would each want satisfying, when in fact one pack finishes the quest and the extra two only raise the Cruor and Resistance Credits. So the three Supply Points are ONE examine rung whose evidence is an alt-list -- holding any one of the three packs proves it -- and the hand-in carries the same three as items OR items_alt. The three key items are distinct, so nothing is duplicated across rungs. The page writes "Supply Points" plural; the singular is recorded as the entity name, and if the live entity turns out to be a bare ??? the rung simply keeps its place and loses its marker. Their three coordinates disagree in a harmless way -- two of the three sit at (F-9) -- so the grid stays null and all three are listed in the note. The Crevice Amoeban and Treacle Slugs are landmarks the page uses to describe where the points are, not things to kill, so they are not recorded as mobs. Morlepiche (A) is given by conflux and not by grid. Fame "aatt" is an Abyssea zone code and gates nothing.
